newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends softer in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends softer in active trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended slightly lower against its American counterpart on Tuesday as the U.S. dollar remained strong in the overseas markets, and dealers said sharp fluctuations were unlikely in the near term.
The local dollar finished at T$27.450 against Monday's T$27.445 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$270 million.

Despite the U.S. dollar's persistent strength overseas, dealers said investors continued to sell U.S. dollar holdings in favour of the local currency to meet liquidity demand ahead of the Chinese lunar new year, which falls on February 7.
The Taiwan dollar buying was not enough to keep the local unit from easing lower, though a further slide was not expected, dealers said.
"It looks like the Taiwan dollar is in a slight downtrend, but this new year-related Taiwan dollar demand should offset the depreciation," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
A T$27.44-27.50 range was seen for Wednesday.
